details.text: A severe threat persists along the KS/MO border. However, the threat should gradually decrease through the evening with strengthening convective inhibition

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A loosely organized MCS continues across northeast KS into western MO. While a few reports of marginally severe hail have been received with cells on the western flank of this MCS, the gusts over the past hour or so have remained below severe limits. As temperatures continue to further cool into the 70s F, boundary-layer decoupling and MLCINH should only increase with time, further diminishing the severe wind threat. A couple of the stronger cells may still pose a hail threat, but severe hail should remain more isolated into the evening hours. Given current severe trends, a downstream WW issuance appears unlikely at this time

statements.headline: Hazardous Weather Outlook
statements.summary: Today and tonight. There is potential for a narrow corridor of training storms producing locally heavy rain overnight tonight that could result in flash flooding, especially if it occurs over areas with still saturated grounds. If confidence increases in a more widespread flash flood threat and confidence in location of that corridor, a Flood Watch may be needed.

details.label: Today's Hazards
details.text: Today and tonight. There is potential for a narrow corridor of training storms producing locally heavy rain overnight tonight that could result in flash flooding, especially if it occurs over areas with still saturated grounds. If confidence increases in a more widespread flash flood threat and confidence in location of that corridor, a Flood Watch may be needed.

details.label: Extended Outlook
details.text: Thursday through Tuesday. Lingering heavy rain Thursday morning could maintain the marginal Flood Risk before exiting the region by Thursday evening. The probability for widespread hazardous weather thereafter is low.
